scope: Only VERBS, ADJECTIVES, ADVERBS constants in specimen_context.py; not the noun/conjunction/relational inventories or whole-source acceptance.
method: Viewed complete original grayscale pages572–575 and each selected occurrence in aligned-clause context; consulted original571 for explicit morphological cautions. No tense/person/voice inference from English translation.

findings.finding: Original p571 explicitly says Iūn, he said, is probably wrong. Current exact specimen occurrence is tagged verb with no qualification.
findings.recommendation: Keep printed iūn and said; add uncertain plus the attributed source warning. Do not silently correct the letters or replace the gloss.

edge_decisions.decision: Printed saying introduces the represented content. Broad nonfinite verbal contextual classification is defensible; the source does not here prove a distinct lexical quotative particle or tense. Do not add either without analysis evidence.
Printed therefore in573 functions adverbially; keep separate from simple iūn said. Do not propagate the questioned-reading warning by substring.
Adjectival contextual reading supported. Keep separate from yaug fitness, which belongs to the noun list and is outside this bounded change.
Occur with following copula was; broad verbal/participial contextual class is defensible but no source morphological tense, passive or lexical adjective claim is established.
Aligned clause supports manner/degree adverb versus attributive adjective respectively; preserve their exact form/gloss-pair scope.
Broad verb compatible with nonfinite/participle function; original571 additionally identifies these forms among participles. No new tense inferred.
